note: What each milestone claims, as data a tool can re-check. `engine_digest` is the digest the ENGINE produces on this install for the milestone's prompt; it is what a cheap re-run can confirm. `agreement` records whether that digest was checked against the CONTRACT, and by which run, because the two are different claims: an engine that reproduces its own recorded digest is stable, and an engine that matches the reference is correct. The M1 confusion came from treating the first as the second. `known_mismatch` is a divergence that has been declared and tracked; anything not declared here fails tools/check_milestones.py, so a new drift cannot arrive quietly.

milestones.claim: the engine's trace is byte-identical to the contract on Qwen3.5-2B over three prompts
milestones.recheck: needs the 2B checkpoint, which is not cached on this machine and must not be fetched to make a gate pass

milestones.claim: the engine's trace on the real 35 B model is byte-identical to a reference contract reading the SAME install -- the falsifiable form of the claim, because the engine reads an install and a contract reading a bf16 checkpoint is a different input, not a different arithmetic
milestones.engine_digest_source: docs/m1-decisions.md, D34's record, and the digest the M2 and M3 gates report for this prompt
milestones.agreement_note: checked 2026-09-17 by running the contract against the install itself (`tools/ordered_qwen36_trace.py .build/m1-install ... --stream-experts`, which reads through the install's own dequantiser, the one the Swift reader mirrors): trace_diff reports IDENTICAL -- 83 tensors, 0 differing elements, 40 discrete decisions, matching digests b0d382dbabf36df0... The earlier 'stale' note said settling it needed a contract run on the checkpoint; the run that settles it is on the install, and D56 explains why that is the right instrument rather than a convenience.
milestones.known_mismatch_note: Against a contract reading the CHECKPOINT the pair differs by 40 discrete decisions and 1 float tensor. That is declared rather than hidden, and it is the measured effect of the install's quantisation (D55: the DeltaNet's three projections and attn.q/k/v/o are int4 in the install and bf16 in the checkpoint, which moves layer 0's attention output by 0.0156 max / 24.5% median relative). DC-112 carries the remaining choice.
